proposal.baseline_comparison: same as control condition; baseline person.recall = 0.211 (MEM-0003), TRUE_DETECTOR_MISS recovery = 1/92 (implied by MEM-0015 comparing yolov8l-oiv7 to YOLO11m), hazard.precision = 0.807 (MEM-0002)
proposal.control_condition: baseline: yolov8m-oiv7, conf=0.4, iou=0.7, imgsz=640, no preprocessing
proposal.dataset_version: Open Images V7 (as used in MEM-0001, MEM-0002, MEM-0003, MEM-0004, MEM-0005)
proposal.hypothesis: The combination of YOLO11m (MEM-0015) and gamma preprocessing (MEM-0014) will recover more than 17/92 TRUE_DETECTOR_MISS Person cases at conf=0.4 by addressing both learned-representation limitations (via architecture shift) and local contrast deficits (via preprocessing), while maintaining hazard precision above 0.757, because gamma preprocessing alone showed a non-significant recall trend (+0.0198) and YOLO11m alone showed recovery potential, suggesting complementary mechanisms.
proposal.implementation_scope: Benchmark evaluation only; requires constructing yolov11m-oiv7.pt and implementing gamma preprocessing in research/evaluation_policy.py inference path
proposal.inconclusive_if: person.recall increase >= 0.03 but hazard.precision < 0.757, or vice versa, or if results are confounded by calibration shifts (per MEM-0021)
proposal.isolation_requirements: Exclude validation image IDs from training manifest via hash comparison; use Open Images V7 official train/val split; no image in val set may appear in training set (verified by SHA256 of filename + ground truth)
proposal.materially_new_rationale: While EXP-0004 tested preprocessing alone and EXP-0005 tested model size alone (both OIV7 vocabulary), this proposal tests a combination of a non-OIV7 checkpoint (YOLO11m, COCO-trained) with a specific preprocessing transform (gamma). This differs from rejected directions because: (1) it involves an architecture family shift (YOLOv8 -> YOLO11), not just backbone size; (2) it combines interventions shown to have individual trends (MEM-0014, MEM-0015); (3) it targets TRUE_DETECTOR_MISS recovery as a specific failure mode, not general recall; and (4) it holds conf=0.4 fixed to avoid the precision collapse seen in EXP-0001.
proposal.model_config_ref: yolov11m (to be constructed; PREREQUISITE: yolov11m-oiv7.pt checkpoint does not yet exist and must be created by converting YOLO11m COCO weights to Open Images V7 601-class vocabulary and fine-tuning on OIV7 training split)
proposal.motivation: MEM-0015 establishes YOLO11m recovers 17/92 TRUE_DETECTOR_MISS cases, but was rejected for production due to precision concerns. MEM-0014 found gamma preprocessing had the strongest effect among tested transforms (+0.0198 recall), though inconclusive. Since EXP-0004 and EXP-0005 showed negligible effects from preprocessing or model size alone, and MEM-0027 notes no combination experiments were run, combining these may yield synergistic gains in TRUE_DETECTOR_MISS recovery while allowing conf=0.4 to be retained, potentially mitigating precision loss seen in EXP-0001.
proposal.procedure: Eval four conditions: (1) yolov8m-oiv7 + no preprocessing (baseline), (2) yolov8m-oiv7 + gamma, (3) yolov11m + no preprocessing, (4) yolov11m + gamma. For each, compute person.recall, hazard.precision, and count of TRUE_DETECTOR_MISS cases recovered (defined as GT with zero detections at conf>=0.4 in baseline but >=1 detection with IoU>=0.5 in condition). Use benchmark/results/baseline/ as fixed GT. Isolate train/eval via image-ID hash exclusion (see isolation_requirements).
proposal.production_impact_description: This proposal evaluates model and preprocessing changes for offline benchmark analysis only. No change to ios/, benchmark/config.py, or baseline run is implied. Any production adoption would require separate human review, retraining on OmniSight-specific data, and validation on-device.
proposal.rejects_hypothesis_if: person.recall increase < 0.03 OR hazard.precision < 0.757 OR TRUE_DETECTOR_MISS recovery <= 17/92
proposal.reproducibility_requirements: Fixed random seed for any stochastic processes; deterministic preprocessing; Open Images V7 validation split hash must match benchmark/results/baseline/; yolov11m-oiv7.pt must be shared via lab-approved artifact registry with SHA256 hash
proposal.research_question: Does combining a YOLO11m checkpoint (different architecture family, COCO-trained) with gamma preprocessing recover more TRUE_DETECTOR_MISS Person cases than either intervention alone, without violating hazard precision guardrails?
proposal.supports_hypothesis_if: person.recall increases by >= 0.03 (to >= 0.241) AND hazard.precision remains >= 0.757 AND TRUE_DETECTOR_MISS recovery increases to > 17/92
proposal.title: Combined YOLO11m checkpoint and gamma preprocessing to recover TRUE_DETECTOR_MISS Person cases

raw_selected_problem: TRUE_DETECTOR_MISS: the model simply never emits any Person detection with sufficient overlap for a given ground truth
raw_selection_rationale: MEM-0003 shows Person recall is 0.211 at conf=0.4, the worst among hazard classes, with GT=303 boxes. MEM-0015 confirms YOLO11m recovered 17/92 (18.5%) TRUE_DETECTOR_MISS cases at conf=0.4, proving recovery is possible via architecture or data changes. This directly addresses the core failure mode where the model emits zero detections for Person GTs, which is distinct from low-confidence or localization failures. Since EXP-0001-0005 tested single interventions (threshold, resolution, class aliasing, preprocessing, model size) and failed to meaningfully improve recall, and MEM-0027 indicates no combined interventions were tested, targeting TRUE_DETECTOR_MISS via a novel combination is justified.
